findings.text: Queue entry for delayed kernel thread work reports success and refuses work when queuing is blocked. On acceptance it delegates to an internal helper while holding worker protection. The helper separates immediate placement from deferred timer based placement.

Modify entry re-arms tracked delayed work with a new delay and reports whether the item had been pending. Items never associated with a worker take a fast path that only queues. Otherwise the current timer is neutralized first, concurrent cancellation short circuits with a pending indication, and the item is removed then requeued.

Synchronous cancellation removes a work item from whichever queue currently holds it and reports removal. Plain and delayed variants share a common helper distinguished by a flag controlling timer neutralization. When the target is the currently executing item the caller waits for completion while blocking new queuing.

Flush for a single work item inserts a temporary marker with a completion after the target when queued, near the head of the ready queue when the target is executing, and does nothing when idle and unqueued. Worker flush appends such a marker at the tail. Both wait for the marker except in the no operation case.
Worker teardown requires an existing thread, drains queued activity, stops the thread, warns if either ready or delayed queues retain entries, then releases the worker object.

Memory context helpers let kernel threads temporarily borrow an address space. The use path takes a reference, switches active and current context under task protection with interrupts suppressed, updates membarrier state, performs the architecture switch, then drops the prior lazy reference. The unuse path orders memory, clears current context, updates membarrier state, takes a lazy reference, enters lazy mode, then drops the main reference.

Block cgroup association stores a subsystem state pointer inside the current kernel thread storage with reference counting, releasing any prior value and acquiring the new one, clearing when given null and ignoring non kernel threads or missing thread storage. The getter returns the stored pointer for kernel threads and null otherwise.

Timer expiry entry detaches the expired item from the delayed collection and promotes it to the ready collection unless cancellation is in progress. It validates that an owning worker exists and matches the recorded owner, warning on misuse.

Each work item remains bound to a single worker for its lifetime. Queue paths record the owner, later operations compare observed and recorded owners and warn on mismatch, and a missing owner on expiry is treated as incorrect reuse after reinitialization.

When no delay is requested placement goes directly to the ready queue for efficiency and timeliness. Otherwise the path runs a sanity check, links the item on the delayed queue, records the owner, computes expiry from current tick count plus the requested delay, then arms the timer.

Worker protection with interrupt state preserved guards ready and delayed membership, owner assignment, cancellation nesting count and current execution pointer across queue, expiry, modify, flush and cancel paths. Timer neutralization and waiting for in progress work temporarily release protection while incrementing the nesting count to block requeuing.

Delayed items progress from never queued to delayed or ready, then to executing and idle. Timer expiry transitions delayed to ready. Cancellation removes from either queued state. Modify neutralizes the timer then requeues. Synchronous cancel waits when the target is in executing state.
Flush helper pairs a generic work item with a completion object. Its callback retrieves the enclosing helper from the work member and signals completion.

Several misuses trigger warnings: expiry without an owner, timer callback identity mismatch, use of one item across workers, destruction with retained ready or delayed entries, and missing thread during teardown.

Scheduler latency accounting discards overly long interruptible waits and durations that do not advance, captures a backtrace for the sleeping task, then merges the sample into a global table and a per task table keyed by full backtrace equality, updating count and totals and maximum on match and allocating a fresh slot otherwise.

Global merging skips threads without user context, scans for identical backtraces terminated by zero, reuses the first empty position for new signatures and drops samples when full. Per task merging follows the same equality rule but stops allocating once a per task save limit is reached.
A global latency spin protection with interrupt state preserved serializes clearing of the global table and all updates to global and per task records.

Latency display emits a version header then a line per occupied global slot showing count, accumulated time and maximum plus symbolic backtrace entries. Writing any data clears the global table and reports the supplied byte count as handled. Opening uses a single open helper and the proc table wires open, read, write, seek and release.

Enable control parses an integer through a generic vector handler then forces scheduler statistics when the flag is set. A control table exposes the flag under a kernel name with owner read write and others read access. Initialization creates a proc entry and registers the control when system control support is present.
Global latency table capacity is 128 slots.
Proc entry name is latency_stats with mode 0644. System control name is latencytop with mode 0644.

Task backtrace capture has two variants. The first acquires a task stack reference, walks the architecture stack with a scheduler skipping consumer, releases the reference and returns collected length, yielding zero when the stack is unavailable. The second builds a trace descriptor with skip adjustment and delegates to a save helper, returning entry count. The fallback save helper only warns as unimplemented.

Module signature validation rejects when declared signature length reaches file length minus footer size, rejects unexpected packet type, rejects any nonzero algorithm, hash, signer length, key identifier length or padding fields, otherwise reports success.

Atomic notifier registration with unique priority and unregistration serialize with interrupt saving spin protection and return the chain result, with unregistration adding a read copy update grace wait. Invocation traverses under read protection. Emptiness checks the head pointer through an access helper.

Blocking notifier registration variants and unregistration bypass the sleeping lock during early boot and otherwise serialize with a write held semaphore. The unique variant requests priority uniqueness.

Sleepable read copy update notifier registration and unregistration bypass the mutex during boot and otherwise serialize with it, with unregistration adding a grace wait. Invocation holds a read lock across traversal. Initialization sets up the mutex and sleepable structure with fatal failure on error and nulls the head.

Die notification builds an argument bundle from trap context, checks read copy update watching state, and dispatches through a global die chain. Registration and unregistration manage membership through atomic chain helpers.

Notifier synchronization differs by flavor. Atomic mutation uses spin with interrupt protection and traversal uses read copy update. Blocking mutation uses a semaphore except during boot. Sleepable mutation uses a mutex except during boot with sleepable read protection for traversal. Unregistration adds the matching grace wait for atomic and sleepable flavors.
Namespace debug helper asserts that each clone type maps to its expected operations table for cgroup, ipc, mount, net, pid, time, user and uts when the corresponding configuration is present.

Memory context helpers warn when the caller is not a kernel thread or has unexpected current context state. Sleepable notifier initialization halts on setup failure. The fallback stack save warns once.
Global latency store is a fixed array of latency records sized by the maximum constant plus an integer enable flag. Clearing zeroes the whole array under protection.
Notifier compilation unit requests trace point instantiation.

Delayed timer cancellation assumes the worker lock is held, bumps the cancellation nesting count, releases the lock, waits for timer callback quiescence, reacquires the lock and unbump. This ordering avoids deadlock with expiry while preventing new queuing.
Interruptible wait discard threshold is 5000 microseconds.
Latency display version label is v0.1.
